walkthroughs.body_html:
Henry VIII became king in 1509 at the age of 17. He needed a son to be his heir — and married six times trying to get one.

The order: Catherine of Aragon (divorced), Anne Boleyn (beheaded), Jane Seymour (died), Anne of Cleves (divorced), Catherine Howard (beheaded), Catherine Parr (survived).

The rhyme: divorced, beheaded, died, divorced, beheaded, survived. 💍

Henry wanted to divorce Catherine of Aragon, but the Pope said no. So Henry made himself Head of the Church of England in 1534.

This was the start of the English Reformation. England left the Catholic Church and became Protestant.

Henry's helper Thomas Cromwell ran the changes through Parliament. ✝️

From 1536 Henry began the Dissolution of the Monasteries. Around 800 monasteries and abbeys were closed.

Their land and treasure went to the king. Many monks lost their homes; books and stained glass were destroyed.

Henry made a fortune — but his daughter Elizabeth would later have to settle the religious arguments he started.

mcqs.q: How did trade unions become legal in 19th-century Britain?
options: Combination Acts banned them until 1824-25 partial repeal; the 1834 Tolpuddle case galvanised opinion; full legal recognition came via Acts in 1871 and 1875.
Trade unions were legalised by Tolpuddle Martyrs being acquitted.
Trade unions were legalised by the 1832 Reform Act.
Magna Carta gave the right to vote to all English men.

mcqs.q: Why is Magna Carta still cited in 'Power and the People' history?
options: Because clauses on lawful judgement and protection from arbitrary imprisonment were reinterpreted in the 17th century to support broader liberties, even though they originally protected only barons.
Magna Carta gave the right to vote to all English men.
Trade unions were legalised by the 1832 Reform Act.
Magna Carta directly created modern human rights in 1215.

mcqs.q: Why was the founding of the NHS controversial in 1948?
options: The NHS was supported by all parties and all doctors from the start.
Trade unions were legalised by the 1832 Reform Act.
The NHS was originally only for soldiers returning from WWII.
The British Medical Association opposed nationalisation of doctors; Bevan made concessions allowing private practice; Conservatives feared cost and central control.
